subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the main role of an operating system?
options: To provide an interface between the user, applications and the computer hardware
To convert high-level source code into binary
To physically store data on the hard disk platters
To supply electrical power to the components
questions.explain: The OS manages communication between the user, software and hardware, providing a platform for programs to run.

questions.q: Which of the following is a function of an operating system?
questions.explain: Managing users and their accounts is one of the recognised functions of an operating system.

questions.q: Which task is NOT normally carried out by the operating system?
options: Translating high-level source code into machine code
questions.explain: Translation is performed by compilers and interpreters, not by the operating system.

questions.q: A user interface that uses windows, icons, menus and pointers is known as a...
questions.explain: A GUI lets users interact with the computer through visual elements such as windows, icons and a mouse pointer.

questions.q: A command line interface (CLI) is best described as an interface where the user...
options: Types text commands to interact with the computer
Uses icons and a mouse pointer to give instructions
Controls the computer entirely by voice
questions.explain: A CLI requires the user to enter typed text commands rather than using graphical elements.

questions.q: What does memory management in an operating system do?
options: Allocates and manages main memory (RAM) for programs and data
Increases the physical capacity of the hard disk
Encrypts every file stored on the system
Cleans dust from the RAM modules
questions.explain: Memory management allocates RAM to programs and data and keeps track of what is stored where.

questions.q: Why does an operating system use multitasking?
options: To allow several applications to appear to run at the same time by sharing CPU time
To increase the clock speed of the processor
To translate programs into machine code
questions.explain: Multitasking rapidly shares processor time between programs so they appear to run simultaneously.

questions.q: A user has a word processor, web browser and music player all open at once. Which OS function allows all three to run apparently simultaneously?
questions.explain: Multitasking lets the OS switch the CPU between programs so they all appear to run at the same time.

questions.q: One purpose of memory management is to ensure that...
options: Programs and data do not overwrite each other in memory
The monitor displays at a higher resolution
The CPU runs at a lower temperature
questions.explain: Memory management keeps programs and their data in separate areas so they do not corrupt one another.

questions.q: A small program that allows the operating system to communicate with a hardware device is called a...
questions.explain: A device driver tells the OS how to communicate with and control a particular piece of hardware.

questions.q: Why does connecting a new printer often require a device driver?
options: The driver tells the OS how to communicate with and control that specific device
The driver supplies electricity to the printer
The driver physically installs the ink cartridges
The driver compresses documents before printing
questions.explain: Each peripheral needs a driver so the operating system knows how to send and receive the correct signals.

questions.q: Which OS function is responsible for organising, storing, retrieving and naming files on secondary storage?
questions.explain: File management handles the naming, storing, retrieving and organising of files and folders.

questions.q: User management in an operating system allows an administrator to...
options: Create user accounts and set access rights and permissions
Increase the amount of RAM installed
Compile source code into machine code
questions.explain: User management controls accounts, log-in details and the access rights each user is given.

questions.q: A school technician wants to stop students deleting certain files while still letting teachers edit them. Which OS function is used?
options: User management, setting access rights and permissions
questions.explain: Access rights and permissions are controlled through the operating system's user management function.

questions.q: What is the purpose of utility software?
options: To help maintain, configure and optimise the computer system
To create documents and spreadsheets for users
To provide the main graphical interface for the user
questions.explain: Utility software performs housekeeping tasks that keep the computer running efficiently and securely.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of utility software named in the specification?
questions.explain: The specification lists encryption, defragmentation and compression software as examples of utility software.

questions.q: What does defragmentation software do on a magnetic hard disk drive?
options: Reorganises fragmented files so they are stored in contiguous blocks, improving access speed
Encrypts the entire contents of the disk
Increases the storage capacity of the disk
questions.explain: Defragmentation gathers scattered file fragments together so the read/write head has less distance to travel.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of encryption software?
options: To scramble data so it cannot be understood without the correct key
To reduce the file size of stored data
To reorganise files on the disk
To manage user accounts and permissions
questions.explain: Encryption software converts data into an unreadable form that can only be decoded with the correct key.

questions.q: What does data compression software aim to do?
options: Reduce the size of files so they take up less storage space
Increase the reliability of the CPU
questions.explain: Compression software reduces file size, saving storage space and speeding up transfer.

questions.q: A magnetic hard disk has become slow because files are scattered in non-contiguous blocks. Which utility should the user run?
questions.explain: Defragmentation reassembles scattered file fragments into contiguous blocks, restoring faster access.
